corroborations.title: Time-series momentum is broad and slow across futures
corroborations.finding: Past 12-month return predicts next month across 58 futures (P727/P327), risk-scaled versions reach Sharpe above 1.2 (P092), commodity futures momentum earns 70-86bp/month (P684), and a replicating model tracks the SocGen Trend Index OOS (P078). P769 explains why: the Sharpe comes from breadth (single market 0.17, 73-market portfolio 0.72).
corroborations.markets: Multi-asset futures: equity indices, bonds, FX, commodities

corroborations.title: Scaling by volatility steadies risk more than it raises Sharpe
corroborations.finding: Variance-scaled portfolios earn alpha (P720: market alpha 4.86% a year) and risk-scaled momentum keeps strategy vol steady (P092). Our own tests agree on the risk side (vol-target validated) but not on a reliable Sharpe gain for a single index (vol-managed-mm underpowered).
corroborations.markets: Equity index, multi-asset futures

corroborations.title: Stops and take-profits rarely improve trend or momentum books
corroborations.finding: No stop configuration improved a trend/ARP book net of costs (P146); ATR stops helped only some MACD models on USDJPY (P026); faster take-profits were not better (P029). P023's stop-loss gains are tied to specific stop-out periods. Our exit-on-fixed-entries test was null on all six exits.
corroborations.markets: Multi-asset, FX, equity index

corroborations.title: Intraday OHLCV breakout and momentum rules die net of costs on futures
corroborations.finding: Two grade-A pre-registered tests find nothing survives: 0/14 MNQ/MGC families (P871) and 0/225 ORB cells (gross +$1.57M, net -$6.49M; P876). Tutorials agree (Dual Thrust Sharpe -0.37 on SPY; Dynamic Breakout II 0.31 on EURUSD). Our close-window and noise-area-book tests match, with the SPY/NQ noise band the only exception.
corroborations.markets: Index and commodity futures, SPY, EURUSD

corroborations.title: Published factor Sharpes shrink once tested honestly
corroborations.finding: FX carry/momentum/value OOS Sharpe fell from +0.39 to -0.32 after publication (P042); Harvey et al. put the bar at t>3.0 and estimate 80-158 of 296 factors are false (P711); naive crypto factor tests inflate Sharpe 3.6x (P015); deflated Sharpe and PBO formalise the haircut (P733, P712).
corroborations.markets: All: equities, FX, crypto, multi-asset

corroborations.title: Carry carries crash risk tied to global volatility
corroborations.finding: High-yield currencies fall when global FX vol spikes (P036); currency carry has skew -1.2, the high-yield sleeve -2.5 (P040); option hedging cuts carry from 6.5% to 1.7-4.8% a year (P721); crash premia explain at most a third of carry (P048).
corroborations.markets: FX (G10 and broader)

contradictions.title: Does simple trend timing on the S&P still work?
contradictions.finding: P679 finds MA timing on S&P beats buy-and-hold over 1860-2014 but not significantly in the second half; P728 finds trend positive in every decade across 67 markets; P540 reports a 200-day rule lifting Sharpe 0.57 to 0.73 over five years.
contradictions.settle: Test single-index MA timing vs multi-market trend on the same 2000-2026 data net of costs: if only the multi-market book works, breadth (P769) explains the gap.
contradictions.our_evidence: trend-following-fx null (FX-only) and portfolio-book context (multi-asset trend sleeve positive); leans to breadth over single-market timing.

contradictions.title: Do stop-losses rescue momentum?
contradictions.finding: P730 says stop-losses turn flat momentum into 2.8%/month in Taiwan (no costs); P146 says no stop improves a trend book net of costs; P768 says the gain comes from regime-dependent weights, not exits.
contradictions.settle: On one multi-asset trend book, compare a stop overlay vs a regime-weight overlay net of costs, both fitted walk-forward.
contradictions.our_evidence: exit-on-fixed-entries null; sides with P146.

contradictions.title: Is US index intraday momentum tradeable?
contradictions.finding: P725 finds the first half hour predicts the last; P716 finds the rest-of-day return predicts the last 30 minutes on 60+ futures; P006 trades a noise-band version at Sharpe 1.33. P871 (grade A) finds no MNQ intraday family survives OOS and costs in 2023-25.
contradictions.settle: Separate the signal shape: first-to-last-half-hour regression trades vs the noise-band breakout, both on NQ 2016-2026 net of real costs.
contradictions.our_evidence: close-window-momentum-trade null (sides with P871 for the half-hour trade); noise-area-momentum underpowered (NQ Sharpe 1.23) and noise-area-momentum-spy validated (sides with P006 for the band rule).

contradictions.title: Are FX carry and momentum premia still alive?
contradictions.finding: P724, P044 and P726 report sizeable currency momentum/carry/value premia; P042 finds OOS Sharpe fell to -0.32 after publication, and P086 (grade A) finds carry best OOS Sharpe -0.25 on four majors.
contradictions.settle: A post-2010 OOS test on the widest currency set we hold (19 crosses incl. EM) net of spread, with enough months to detect Sharpe 0.3.
contradictions.our_evidence: fx-factor-carry underpowered (right sign), fx-factor-momentum underpowered (wrong sign), trend-following-fx null; leans to P042 but not settled.

contradictions.title: Does deep learning beat linear momentum?
contradictions.finding: Deep momentum networks claim more than 2x Sharpe over TSMOM (P624, P298) and X-Trend ~10x (P632); P285 finds one-layer linear models beat transformers by 20-50% MSE and argues such gains need a linear baseline.
contradictions.settle: Run a regularised linear multi-lookback trend model beside a small LSTM on the same futures, walk-forward with costs.
contradictions.our_evidence: none directly; meta-label-yield-spread null and noise-area-build null suggest added model complexity has not helped on our data.

contradictions.title: Does vol-managing raise Sharpe or just cut risk?
contradictions.finding: P720 reports alphas from variance scaling across factors; P805 finds volatility risk carries a negative premium, and P788 shows significant Sharpes often cannot be told apart statistically, so claimed Sharpe gains may be noise.
contradictions.settle: Test vol-managed vs unmanaged on each sleeve with a formal Sharpe-difference test and separately on drawdown.
contradictions.our_evidence: vol-managed-mm underpowered (NQ Sharpe diff -0.006, best drawdown) and vol-target validated on steadier risk; sides with risk reduction, not Sharpe gain.

themes.label: Gold, commodities, sentiment & cross-asset
themes.summary: The strongest material in this pack is about who holds commodity futures and what their trading does to price (COT flow and hedger shocks), and about gold as a regime-dependent asset that trades with bonds and the dollar rather than with fear. The best combinations pair a weekly COT flow signal with the desk's own validated crowding-reset state and vol-target sizing, and a gold trend rule filtered by a duration trend and sized by a simple HAR or GVZ forecast. Commodity curve-carry and Goldman-roll ideas look good on paper, but the desk holds no futures term structures, so they wait on data. The sentiment, Twitter and crypto papers are mostly grade C, or are on data we do not hold. The pack and our Evidence Book agree that simple linear vol models beat machine learning, and that ML or sentiment direction claims shrink badly out of sample.

blueprints.name: COT flow-orthogonal commodity momentum
blueprints.idea: Each week, split every commodity's return into the part explained by speculators' net trading and the part left over. Go with the left-over part for one week, and lean against the flow-driven part. Scale each market to equal risk, and give extra weight in weeks with a large hedger (PMPU) positioning shock.
blueprints.market: US commodity futures (energy, metals, grains, softs, livestock) plus gold, via the COT price panel
blueprints.horizon: weekly (Tuesday-to-Tuesday), with a 4-12 week hedger-shock overlay

parts.why: The core signal: return orthogonal to non-commercial net trading predicts the next week (+11.6 bp per 1 sd, ~6.2% a year on 26 North American futures), and the flow-driven part reverses.

Grade A, pre-registered. First-week |z|>1.5 sigma PMPU hedger shocks across 12 commodities carry signed information, with only the 12-week horizon passing every gate. Use the shock weeks as timing and conviction, not as a standalone signal.

Explains why hedger position changes are not pure hedging (position-change vol 0.5-0.7 vs 0.07 for output), so the price-responsive part of positioning should be stripped out, which is exactly what P764 does.

Spectral law for futures books: diversification across many markets buys Sharpe far faster than convexity (single-market Sharpe 0.17 to portfolio 0.72), so run it as a broad equal-risk book, not on a few contracts.

blueprints.mechanism_fit: All three positioning papers describe the same thing: speculators' trading pushes price for a while, then that push fades, while the information-driven part of the move persists. Splitting the return by flow is the clean way to separate the two, and a broad, vol-scaled book is the way to collect a small weekly edge.
blueprints.data_note: COT at full depth, 36 markets weekly from 2006 (R2 archive, B8), with the price series the COT crowding programme already used; disaggregated PMPU and TFF in the feature store.

evidence.bearing: Positioning LEVEL ranked against its own history did not predict returns. This design uses weekly FLOW to decompose the return instead, which that test did not try.
Same family, same holdout markets: a pullback while the crowd leaves is followed by the trend resuming. This supports the idea that flow-driven moves fade, and it can serve as a confirmation leg.
Adding COT features to a price/vol/macro classifier made adverse-move prediction worse. The blueprint must beat a price-only weekly reversal or momentum baseline, not just zero.
Vol-target sizing steadies risk and lifted the trend sleeve. Use it for the equal-risk book.

blueprints.risk: The edge is ~12 bp a week before costs, and the commodity futures roll cost and spread on CFDs may eat most of it.
blueprints.first_test: On the 22-market COT holdout panel 2006-2026, regress next-week return on last week's flow-orthogonal return. Compare the pooled weekly IC and net Sharpe with a plain one-week own-return momentum or reversal benchmark and a shuffled-flow placebo.

blueprints.name: Gold-plus-duration trend with HAR/GVZ sizing
blueprints.idea: Hold gold long only when both gold and Treasury duration (IEF or the 10y yield falling) have positive 12-month returns, and stay flat or in cash otherwise. Size the position by a HAR or GVZ volatility forecast so the monthly risk stays constant.
blueprints.market: XAU/USD (OANDA CFD) or GC

parts.why: The joint gold and IEF 12-month trend state lifts GLD's Sharpe to 0.59, and to 0.81 with cash earning Fed funds, at a similar drawdown. It is the rates leg of gold expressed as a filter.
Gold hedges stocks on average and acts as a safe haven only in extreme falls. This argues for keeping the filter on the bond and rates leg rather than adding an equity-fear trigger.
On 20 years of weekly COMEX gold, HAR-RV beats a COT/psychophysics random forest out of sample (R2 0.313 vs 0.125). Use plain HAR for gold vol.
Across 47 futures, EWMA vol scaled below the sqrt(h) rule explains ~40-45% of future realised vol. This gives a simple fallback forecast and the right horizon scaling for a monthly hold.

blueprints.mechanism_fit: Gold mostly trades as a real-rate and dollar asset, so requiring the duration trend to agree selects the 'rates gold' state. Vol-target sizing then cuts the drawdown without needing any direction skill.
blueprints.data_note: OANDA gold M1/daily 2002+, Yahoo long dailies (credit/duration ETFs, ^TNX from 1970), the US curve, GVZ in the Cboe family, the gold IV ladder.

evidence.bearing: Gold follows real yields or the dollar in only about half of the windows, and 'neither' drives it 45% of the time. A duration-trend filter is a direct way to trade only in the rates-gold windows.
A 13-market slow trend book was 'carried by yen crosses, gold and NAS100'. That makes gold the most promising single leg, but the book itself was not proven.
GVZ-based sigma beats the realised ladder for gold. It is a ready sizing input.
Forecast-sigma sizing buys a smaller worst month at the same Sharpe. That is the expected gain from the sizing slot.
A competing macro-state filter for gold failed correction. The duration-trend filter is cheaper, so race the two.

blueprints.risk: The 12-month joint state switches rarely, so 20 years give few independent regimes, and the gain over buy-and-hold may sit inside the noise (like slow-bias-clock-book).
blueprints.first_test: Monthly from 2003 to 2026 on XAU/USD net of CFD financing, compare the joint gold-and-IEF 12-month state rule with gold-only 12-month trend and with buy-and-hold (Sharpe 0.64, DD -27% per overnight-hold-gold), at equal vol. Report the Sharpe difference CI and the max drawdown.

blueprints.name: Hedger-shock to producer-sector 12-week tilt
blueprints.idea: When the hedger (PMPU) net position in crude, natgas, metals or grains jumps by more than 1.5 sigma in a week, take a signed 12-week position in the matching producer sector ETF (XLE, XLB) rather than in single stocks. Run it as a pre-registered event book with a placebo on shifted weeks.
blueprints.market: Sector ETFs XLE/XLB (and mega-cap producers if held), signalled by commodity COT
blueprints.horizon: 12 weeks (the only horizon that passed all of P731's gates)

parts.why: Grade A pre-registered result: hedger shocks predict signed producer-equity CAR, and the 12-week IR of 1.01 passes all four gates, including the shift placebo.
Strip out the speculator-flow-driven part of the contemporaneous commodity move before signing the shock, so the trade follows information rather than flow that will reverse.
Its audit inflated Sharpe 3.6x on average under naive evaluation. Count every commodity-horizon cell as a trial and deflate.

blueprints.mechanism_fit: Producers hedge when they learn something about their own output or costs, so a sudden hedger shock is a slow-diffusing signal about producer cash flows. Equities absorb that over weeks, whereas futures are priced quickly.
blueprints.data_note: COT disaggregated PMPU is held. Sector ETFs XLE/XLB daily are held in the 30-series panel. Single-stock producer returns (36 firms) are mostly not held.

evidence.bearing: The same COT data showed no predictive power on the futures themselves. The blueprint targets a different asset (equities) at a 12-week lag, which that test did not cover.
Positioning carries information about who must act. That is consistent with hedger shocks being informative rather than noise.

blueprints.risk: With only ~700 shocks over 12 commodities and 12-week overlapping holds, the sector-ETF version may be underpowered, and only 4 of 36 of P731's cells survived the cluster bootstrap.
blueprints.first_test: On 2006-2026, compute the 12-week XLE return after first-week |z|>1.5 crude/natgas PMPU shocks, signed by the shock. Compare it with the same signed return on 200 shifted-week placebos and with the XLE drift.

blueprints.name: Carry-conditioned multi-asset trend with crash-state scaling
blueprints.idea: Run a risk-scaled time-series momentum book over commodities, metals, indices, bonds and FX. Only take trend positions that carry agrees with (or does not oppose), and cut exposure in 'panic' states (after market falls with high vol), when momentum crashes.
blueprints.market: Multi-asset: the 30-series daily panel (indices, sectors, gold, silver, copper, WTI, FX, TLT, BTC) plus COT price series

parts.why: Time-series momentum across 71 futures at monthly, weekly and daily frequency, with risk-scaled Sharpe reported above 1.2. This is the base engine.
Conditioning trend on carry across 83 futures (36 of them commodities) raises Sharpe, e.g. equity trend 0.73 to 0.87, and keeps tracking error to pure trend at ~5.5%.
Momentum crashes cluster after declines in high vol, and a dynamic version roughly doubles Sharpe. Use it as the exposure cut.
Breadth drives Sharpe. Per its spectral law, the book needs many uncorrelated markets, which is why the commodities matter.

blueprints.mechanism_fit: Trend collects slow-moving risk premia and under-reaction, carry tells you whether holding the trend is paid or costs you, and the crash state marks when trend's short-gamma tail bites. The three describe one book with an entry filter and a risk throttle.
blueprints.data_note: Daily prices are held for 30 series and the COT markets. Commodity carry needs futures curves, which are not held (FX carry from rate differentials and bond carry from curves are held).

evidence.bearing: FX-only trend is null, and broad multi-asset trend only ~0.3 OOS. That makes adding commodities and carry conditioning the point, not more FX.
A Carver trend+carry blend on 7 USD crosses could not detect realistic gains. Test on a wide panel instead, or the result will be underpowered again.
The trend sleeve alone was Sharpe 0.26 inside the desk's book. That is the incumbent to beat.
Scaling trend by COT crowding added nothing. The crash-state throttle here is price and vol based, a different overlay.

blueprints.risk: Without commodity curves the carry leg covers only FX and bonds, and the post-2009 trend Sharpe of ~0.3 leaves little room for an overlay to show.
blueprints.first_test: On the 30-series panel 2006-2026, compare risk-scaled 12-month TSMOM with and without the panic-state cut (trailing 24-month market return < 0 and 1-month vol in its top quintile). Report the net Sharpe difference and worst-month change, with the current trend sleeve as the benchmark.
related: Multi-asset trend book with regime-dependent weights
Multi-asset trend with a panic-state brake

blueprints.name: Geopolitical-shock gold sleeve in loose conditions
blueprints.idea: Use the GPR index's threats and acts components, orthogonalised to the VIX, to tilt a gold sleeve long after a 1 sd geopolitical shock. Do it only when financial conditions (NFCI) are loose and GPR is rising. Size by the HAR gold vol forecast and hold 1-4 months.
blueprints.market: XAU/USD

parts.why: Per 1 sd shock, gold rises 0.45% for threats (month 0) and 0.60% for acts (month 4), roughly doubling in the rising-GPR and loose-FCI regimes. This is the signal, though grade C and in-sample.
In commodity factor pricing, NFCI carries a significant risk premium (-0.51, SE 0.01) while the VIX does not. That supports a financial-conditions regime rather than a fear gauge.
HAR-RV is the best gold vol forecast in the pack, so use it to keep the sleeve at constant risk.

blueprints.mechanism_fit: The geopolitical demand for gold is reserve and insurance buying, separate from the VIX fear trade, and it shows up more when money is loose. Orthogonalising to the VIX is exactly the leg our fear-gold test did not isolate.
blueprints.data_note: The GPR history is archived (data map: 'never touched'), NFCI is on FRED (untested), and gold is from OANDA.

evidence.bearing: VIX spikes were followed by gold lagging over 20 days (-1.19%). P153's shock is orthogonal to the VIX, so this is the untested 'reserve/geopolitical gold', not the failed fear gold.
Reserve gold is the residual and 'cannot be confirmed from a free feed'. GPR is a candidate observable for it.
Another narrative gold driver was null with an MDE of 1.8%. The 0.45-1.0% effects here are smaller, so power is the first worry.

blueprints.risk: Effects of 0.45-1.0% a month on ~430 monthly observations are likely below the detectable size, and GPR is revised and news-count based.
blueprints.first_test: On monthly data from 1990 to 2026, regress next 1-4 month gold returns on the VIX-orthogonalised GPR threats and acts shocks, with an NFCI-loose interaction. Benchmark against gold's own drift and a shifted-month placebo, and report the MDE first.

blueprints.name: Commodity curve carry with inventory regime and roll timing
blueprints.idea: Rank commodities on basis and basis momentum each month, going long backwardated, improving-curve markets and short the opposite. Take more risk when inventories are low. Time entries around the GSCI roll window (5th-9th business day), when index rolls distort front spreads.
blueprints.market: US commodity futures (energy first)
blueprints.horizon: monthly, with a daily roll-window overlay

parts.why: Curve-surface basis and basis-momentum predictors earn 11.9% (t=3.16) and 8.3% (t=2.80) a year HML. Basis momentum has an OOS R2 of 15.83%.
Theory of storage: low inventories predict backwardation and higher momentum and basis returns. This is the state variable for when carry pays.
The Goldman roll depresses calendar spreads in the 5th-9th business-day window. Front-running it earned Sharpe 2.2 on energy, so avoid entering into the window, or trade against it.
Chinese commodity evidence shows high-frequency versions cannot cover costs. Keep this monthly.

blueprints.mechanism_fit: Basis is the price of storage and hedging pressure, inventories decide how big that premium is, and the index roll is a predictable flow that temporarily bends the same curve. All three act on one object, the futures term structure.
blueprints.data_note: No futures term structures (2nd-6th contracts) are held. Only front or continuous prices for WTI, copper, gold, silver and the COT markets. The roll-window leg needs front and next contracts. Inventories would need EIA/USDA pulls.

evidence.bearing: The only curve-like energy test on the desk (crack spread) found nothing for range. It says nothing about carry direction.

blueprints.risk: Without curve data it cannot be built, and P752 finds the opposite sign for spot-anchored basis in China, so the definition matters.
blueprints.first_test: Pull front and second-month settles for ~20 US commodities (2006-2026) and compute the monthly HML on the front-minus-second basis. Compare it with an equal-weight long commodity benchmark and a sign-flipped placebo before any CNN or inventory layer.

blueprints.name: State-dependent commodity-currency link
blueprints.idea: Trade AUD, CAD and NZD after large moves in their export commodity (copper or iron proxy, WTI, dairy proxy), but only in the risk and carry state where the link is known to switch on. Size by HAR FX vol.
blueprints.market: AUD/USD, USD/CAD, NZD/USD (plus NOK if held)

parts.why: A 1% export-price shock lifts the currency ~2 bp at once, peaking at ~+10 bp over a month, and the size and sign depend on the risk/carry state.
Carry-unwind responses switch on only in high-vol states (Holm p 0.010-0.018). This is the state definition to borrow.
HAR-RV, a simple FX vol forecast, for constant-risk sizing.

blueprints.mechanism_fit: Commodity currencies price terms of trade, but when risk appetite or carry positioning dominates, that channel is swamped. Conditioning on the vol and carry state is the shared idea of both direction-side papers.
blueprints.data_note: FX M1 is held, and WTI, copper and gold daily are held. Country export price indices are not, so a proxy has to be built from held commodities. VIX and FX IV states are held.

evidence.bearing: Unconditional oil-to-CAD and copper-to-AUD after big moves show no 5-day lead (MDE 0.23-0.36 sigma). The state-conditioning is the new part, but it also cuts the sample.
Crude round trips did not drag USD/CAD back. A warning that the intraday link is noisy.
The carry-unwind shape on the desk was too rare to score (35 episodes). Expect the same sample problem for high-vol states.

blueprints.risk: A ~10 bp monthly effect is far below the desk's measured MDE for single-pair direction, so it will likely be underpowered unless pooled across many exporters.
blueprints.first_test: Pool AUD, CAD and NZD 2006-2026 and regress the next 20-day currency return on the 20-day proxy export-price change, interacted with a high-VIX state. Compare against the unconditional slope and a shifted-date placebo, and state the MDE.

blueprints.name: Gold as a crash-only hedge sleeve
blueprints.idea: Add gold to an equity-heavy book only as a tail hedge, sized up when equities are in an extreme-fall state and scaled back afterwards (gold lost its safe-haven role in COVID Phase II). Judge it on expected shortfall, not return.
blueprints.market: XAU/USD against NAS100/SPX500

parts.why: Gold is a safe haven only at extreme stock-fall quantiles (US total effect -0.0183 at 1%). This defines the state.
Gold was a safe haven in COVID Phase I but lost it in Phase II (gold-equity correlation +0.21 to +0.27). The hedge must switch off once the panic turns into a liquidity scramble.
Gold rose in 8 of 11 major S&P drawdowns, with near-zero average stock correlation. This is the base rate for a hedge sleeve.

blueprints.mechanism_fit: All three treat gold's equity link as state-dependent: near zero on average, negative only in sharp falls, and unreliable in forced selling. That fits a conditional hedge, not a direction call.
blueprints.data_note: OANDA gold and index CFD M1/daily, the VIX family, and the desk's portfolio-book harness.

evidence.bearing: After VIX spikes gold lagged its drift by 1.19% over 20 days. Any hedge sleeve must be short-dated or it gives the protection back.
VIX to gold was the strongest 'Faint' pair (+0.218 sigma over 5 days, misses BH only). This supports a short-horizon window.
The desk already validates a tail-ES hedge test design (-9.2% ES5). Reuse that yardstick for gold.

blueprints.risk: Gold sold off with equities in the liquidity phases of 2008 and March 2020, exactly when the hedge is needed.
blueprints.first_test: On 2006-2026 daily data, hold gold at equal risk against a long NAS100 book only on days after NAS100 sits in its bottom 5% daily return, for 5 sessions. Compare the book's daily ES5 with an always-on gold hedge and with 200 random same-size hedges (the hedge-finder-book-es design).

blueprints.name: High-vol intraday hedging-demand momentum on futures
blueprints.idea: On high-vol days only, trade the last 30 minutes before the close in the direction of the rest-of-day return on liquid futures (index, then gold and crude). This is the dealer and hedger rebalancing flow. Run it only where futures costs are a tick.
blueprints.market: ES/NQ futures first; GC/CL only if futures minute data are held

parts.why: Across 60+ futures (21 commodities), 1974-2020, the rest-of-day return predicts the last 30 minutes, tied to hedging demand (equity t=4.43-6.46).
Chinese commodity intraday momentum is OOS-positive only in the high-vol subsample. This is the regime gate.
Intraday commodity momentum cannot cover costs. Futures-only, one trade a day, at most.

blueprints.mechanism_fit: Hedgers who are short gamma or rebalancing must trade in the move's direction late in the day, and that pressure is largest when the day has moved a lot in high vol.
blueprints.data_note: NT8 futures minute data for ES/NQ/YM/RTY are held. Gold and crude futures intraday may only be in the new footprint feed. Gold CFD M1 is held but its spread is too wide.

evidence.bearing: Vol-scaled close-window momentum is null on NQ/ES 2016-2026. Only a high-vol-tercile pointer (+0.025 slope) was left 'for a new prereg on unseen data', and that is the only angle here.
The gold settle window shows nothing (+0.007) and loses 2.5 bp net. Do not run the gold leg on CFDs.
Gold intraday momentum gross (0.8-1.1 bp/day) is below the spread. That confirms the cost wall.

blueprints.risk: The high-vol pointer came from 2020 and 2022 alone, so it may be an artefact of two years.
blueprints.first_test: Pre-register the top-trailing-vol-tercile slope on NQ/ES futures for the 2026-08-22 onward lockbox and forward record. The benchmark is the all-days slope and 1 tick of cost, with a pass bar of a slope of at least 0.025 and net of at least 1 bp.
related: Late-day index momentum on volatile mornings

corroborations.title: Simple linear vol models beat machine learning
corroborations.finding: Independent tests on gold futures (HAR R2 0.313 vs RF 0.125), FX (HAR beats ARFIMA and RiskMetrics), 47 futures (EWMA scaling explains ~40-45%), S&P 100 stocks (HAR best RMSE and QLIKE vs NHITS, TFT, LSTM), Bitcoin quantiles (linear base models win) and long-horizon series (one-layer linear beats Transformers) all find that the simple cascade or linear model wins out of sample.
corroborations.markets: gold, FX, multi-asset futures, single stocks, crypto

corroborations.title: Positioning follows price; the flow-driven part fades
corroborations.finding: Speculator flow's contemporaneous price push reverses (P764: the flow coefficient is negative next week, while the flow-orthogonal return persists). Surveyed lead-lag tests find price leads positions, not the reverse (P729). Hedger position changes track price and other non-output motives (P125), and COT positions correlate with price (P862). Together they say positioning is mostly a reaction, and only the residual carries information.
corroborations.markets: US commodity futures

corroborations.title: Time-series momentum is pervasive in futures including commodities
corroborations.finding: Six papers on 64-83 futures panels find trend profits across asset classes: Sharpe above 1.2 risk-scaled (P092), 70-86 bp/month in futures momentum (P684), network momentum Sharpe 1.5 (P653), and a portfolio Sharpe of 0.72 from single-market 0.17 through breadth (P769). Carry and regime conditioning add 0.15-0.23 Sharpe (P145, P768). Our own OOS is weaker (multi-asset ~0.3, FX null), so breadth and commodities, not FX, are where it lives.
corroborations.markets: multi-asset futures, commodities

corroborations.title: Gold's link to equities is regime-dependent
corroborations.finding: Gold hedges stocks on average but is a safe haven only in extreme falls (P094). It lost safe-haven status in COVID Phase II (P795), rose in 8 of 11 drawdowns but with near-zero average correlation (P147), and timing works better when conditioned on the bond trend (P753) or an entropy regime (P748). None supports a constant gold-equity relationship. Our which-gold and fear-gold results agree.
corroborations.markets: gold vs US/EU/Asian equity indices and Treasuries

corroborations.title: Backtest Sharpe in crypto and ML is heavily inflated
corroborations.finding: Naive evaluation inflates crypto factor Sharpe 3.6x, and no factor survives deflation (P015, grade A). Adversarial checks collapse an in-sample Sharpe of ~13 (P738). Trial-count commitment (P736) and overfitting probability (P586) are needed. An LLM's validation IC of 0.055-0.065 fell to 0.020 on blind data (P825). Any crypto, sentiment or ML blueprint should expect a large haircut.
corroborations.markets: crypto perps, single stocks (LLM)

contradictions.title: Do financial investors move commodity prices?
contradictions.finding: P686 finds the GSCI roll depresses spreads in a predictable window (energy front-run Sharpe 2.2), and P787 links hedge-fund OI share to a +4% equity-commodity DCC. P796 says index rolls have little price impact, and P729 says speculators are liquidity providers whose positions follow price.
contradictions.settle: Measure the front-minus-second spread change in business days 5-9 against the other days of the month, on 2006-2026 settles for energy. Separately, test whether weekly COT flow Granger-leads price after controlling for lagged price.
contradictions.our_evidence: cot-positioning-factor null (positioning level does not predict), which leans toward P729/P796 for direction. The roll-window question is untested here.

contradictions.title: Are hedger COT shocks information or noise?
contradictions.finding: P731 (grade A) treats PMPU shocks as signed information for producer equities. P125 shows hedger positions move far more than output risk warrants and track price, so the shock is partly non-informational. The hedging-pressure strategy (P501) assumes a clean signal.
contradictions.settle: Split each PMPU shock into a price-explained part and a residual (as P764 does for speculators), and test whether only the residual predicts 12-week producer returns.
contradictions.our_evidence: positioning-into-release-direction validated (positioning shows who must act). cot-positioning-factor null (no level signal). The residual split is untested.

contradictions.title: Is gold a safe haven?
contradictions.finding: P094 and P147 find gold protective in extreme equity falls (up in 8 of 11 S&P drawdowns). P715 calls gold unreliable as a hedge, and P795 finds the safe-haven role vanished in COVID Phase II.
contradictions.settle: Condition on horizon and type of stress: gold's 1-5 day and 20-day return after the bottom 1-5% equity days, split into liquidity-scramble episodes (high dollar funding stress) and other episodes.
contradictions.our_evidence: fear-gold null: gold lags by 1.19% over 20 days after VIX spikes, siding with P715/P795 at a month. relationship-map underpowered: VIX to gold +0.218 sigma at 5 days ('Faint'), a short-horizon nod to P094.

contradictions.title: Does intraday momentum survive in futures?
contradictions.finding: P716 (60 futures, 1974-2020), P725 (SPY) and P874 (Chinese commodities, high-vol subsample) find that the early-day return predicts the last half hour. P867 finds intraday commodity momentum cannot cover costs.
contradictions.settle: A pre-registered high-vol-tercile test on unseen post-2026-08 futures data, net of one tick.
contradictions.our_evidence: close-window-momentum null on NQ/ES 2016-2026 (sides with P867 for our era). close-window-momentum-secondary context: gold null and net-negative.

contradictions.title: Do sentiment and ML models beat the random walk in FX?
contradictions.finding: Twitter regARIMA (P647, P649) and a Transformer (P646, Sharpe above 1.8 gross) claim to beat the random walk on EUR/USD and majors. A one-layer linear model beats Transformers, including on the exchange-rate dataset (P285), and a crowd platform loses to the random walk on FX (P650).
contradictions.settle: Run each claimed model walk-forward against both the random walk and a linear direct multi-step baseline, net of spread, on 2016-2026 FX.
contradictions.our_evidence: bias-learner-fx null and cb-tone-direction null (central bank tone priced within 30 minutes, no next-day lean). Both side with P285/P650.

contradictions.title: What sign does commodity basis carry?
contradictions.finding: P751 (and the storage theory in P862) finds basis and basis momentum predict positive returns (HML 11.9%, t=3.16). P752 finds spot-anchored basis signals predict negative returns in Chinese futures (SB -1.50%/month, t=-3.10), with the standard basis-momentum leg weak (+0.85%, t=1.69).
contradictions.settle: Compute both futures-anchored and spot-anchored basis on the same US commodity panel and period, and check whether the sign flips with the anchor or with the market.
contradictions.our_evidence: none
